sections.h2: Where is the Charlevoix County Register of Deeds and how do I reach it?
sections.html:
The Charlevoix County Register of Deeds sits at 13513 Division Street in the city of Charlevoix, MI 49720. The state treasury list of registers of deeds gives the phone as 231-547-7204 and the fax as 231-237-0106, and the office takes email at rod@charlevoixcounty.org. Call before you drive in, because the office page does not post public counter hours.

Charlevoix is the county seat, and Boyne City is the largest city. Anyone selling a house in the county, whether it is a Lake Charlevoix cottage, a place in East Jordan, or a home on Beaver Island, finishes the transfer at this one office. The county Register of Deeds page describes the office as a constitutional office created in 1835 that records, indexes and preserves land documents.

sections.h2: What happens to my deed once Charlevoix County receives it?
sections.html:
Staff stamp the time on it, give it a liber and page, scan it and add it to the searchable index. That sequence is what puts the buyer's name on the public record for the property.

The office is plain about its limits. Its page says recording does not make a document legal; it makes the document public. Counter staff have no blank deed forms to hand out and cannot draft or coach, because MCL 600.916(1) bars clerks from legal advice. Your closing attorney or the title agent prepares the deed, and the register of deeds only checks it against the recording rules.

  • Deeds, mortgages, land contracts and discharges are recorded here.
  • The computer image index reaches back to January 1984, and older records are still being indexed.
  • Documents can be walked in or mailed with the fee and a prepaid return envelope.

sections.h2: What are the Charlevoix County recording charges?
sections.html:
Filing one document costs $30.00 whatever its length. That amount follows MCL 600.2567, and the county fee page notes that $4.00 of it is sent to the Michigan State Survey and Remonumentation Fund.

Charlevoix County Register of Deeds statutory fees (county fee page)
ItemCharge
Recording one document$30.00
Each extra liber and page on an assignment or discharge covering several instruments$3.00
Tax certification$5.00
Copies of documents$1.00 a page
Plat copies$4.00 a page
Certified copy$5.00

One check payable to the Charlevoix County Register of Deeds can cover the recording fee, any transfer tax and the tax certification together. Since January 2, 2025, the office adds $3.00 per document for return postage when you send a document in without a prepaid return envelope, and it holds the document unrecorded until that amount arrives.

sections.h2: What transfer tax comes due at a Charlevoix County closing?
sections.html:
Most sales carry two taxes, both counted in $500 slices of the price with any leftover treated as a full slice. MCL 207.504 sets the county rate at 55 cents a slice for counties under 2,000,000 people. MCL 207.525 sets the state rate at $3.75 a slice.

Take a sale at $276,800, the Census median value for homes that owners live in here. That is 554 slices, so roughly $305 in county tax and $2,078 in state tax. The deed has to print the full value on its face, or an affidavit stating it rides along.

Some transfers escape the county tax. MCL 207.505 lists instruments with consideration under $100, security instruments such as mortgages, leases, and deeds that only fix a title flaw. Check with the office on how your own deed is treated well before the closing date.

sections.h2: Which layout rules can bounce a deed at the Charlevoix counter?
sections.html:
A deed must satisfy the page rules in MCL 565.201, and the office may not take one that misses them. Formatting causes most returns, so inspect the sheet before it goes in the mail.

  • Margin: 2.5 inches of clear space at the head of page one and half an inch around the rest of every page.
  • Print: 10-point type or bigger, black ink, white paper of 20-pound stock or heavier.
  • Size: letter or legal sheets only, from 8.5 by 11 up to 8.5 by 14.
  • First line: one statement naming the recordable event, such as warranty deed.
  • Only one recordable event per instrument.

The statute also wants a legible printed name under every signature that matches the acknowledgment, and the drafter's name and business address on anything signed after 1964.

sections.h2: Why do I need a tax certificate before a warranty deed is recorded in Charlevoix County?
sections.html:
Michigan law makes the office ask for proof that no tax liens attach to the parcel. Under MCL 211.135 the county treasurer certifies that taxes for the five years leading up to the deed date are paid, and Charlevoix charges $5.00 for that certification.

The county fee page names the deeds that trigger this step: warranty deeds, covenant deeds, land contracts, and trustee, fiduciary or personal representative deeds with a warranty clause. It also covers master deeds for condominiums. A quitclaim deed with no warranty covenants is excluded by MCL 211.135(6)(e), so it moves through without the certificate. Start at the County Treasurer's Office first, then bring the certificate with the deed.

sections.h2: How can I search records or guard my title in Charlevoix County?
sections.html:
The county offers three search routes and a free fraud alert. Webtecs is the free portal for taxpayers and occasional users, and images can be bought document by document. Laredo Anywhere is a subscription service for people who run title searches regularly, and the office asks for an email to rod@charlevoixcounty.org to request an agreement. Tapestry is a web search that needs no subscription.

Homeowners can also sign up for Property Fraud Alert, which emails the owner when a document is recorded under their name. That helps after a sale too, since a seller can watch for a deed or lien appearing against a property they believed they had cleared.

sections.h2: How does Charlevoix County's housing stock look in federal data?
sections.html:
Charlevoix County is one of the pricier corners of northern Michigan. The Census Bureau counts 26,036 residents in 2025 and 18,026 housing units. Owners live in 83.5% of occupied homes, median rent is $949, and the typical household brings in $76,531 (2020 to 2024 survey years).

In the 2020 count, 35.4% of housing units sat vacant, which points to plenty of seasonal and second homes. Builders took out 111 permits in 2025. Water covers 70% of the county's 1,390 square miles, and the 416 square miles of land make it the fourth smallest county in Michigan by land area, so waterfront parcels and island properties often carry details that the deed and title search have to capture accurately.

faqs.q: What is the filing charge for one deed in Charlevoix County?
faqs.a: One document costs $30.00 whatever its length. A tax certification adds $5.00 when the deed type calls for one, and a mailed document with no prepaid return envelope adds $3.00 for postage. Transfer tax is separate and follows the sale price.

faqs.q: Can the Charlevoix County office prepare my deed for me?
faqs.a: No. Staff cannot draft papers or give legal advice, since MCL 600.916(1) bars clerks from it, and the office keeps no blank deed forms. Have an attorney or the title agent prepare the deed first.

faqs.q: Do I need a tax certificate for a quitclaim deed in Charlevoix County?
faqs.a: Usually not. MCL 211.135(6)(e) exempts a quitclaim deed or other conveyance with no covenants of warranty from the certificate rule. Warranty deeds, covenant deeds, land contracts and certain fiduciary deeds do need the County Treasurer's certification first.

faqs.q: How do I pay the transfer tax on a Charlevoix County sale?
faqs.a: Pay it at the time of recording. The fee page asks that transfer tax and tax certification checks be made out to the Charlevoix County Register of Deeds, and one check can cover them together with the recording fee. Rates are 55 cents (county) and $3.75 (state) per $500 slice.

faqs.q: Where can I buy a copy of a recorded Charlevoix deed?
faqs.a: Search the free Webtecs portal and buy the image, or ask the office. The fee page lists plain copies at $1.00 a page and certified copies at $5.00, so request the exact total on a long document.
